proposals.relationship: Philip J. Deloria draws on Wilson’s account of oral tradition’s contextual rules and review by knowledgeable audiences when explaining its historical legitimacy (2002).
proposals.evidence_note: A specifically credited methodological resource in Deloria’s own chapter, not a claim of personal mentoring or a general career lineage. He cites Wilson’s 1997 essay, whose body remains unread here; the 1996 essay is a distinct work.
primary_locators: Historiography, printed p. 16, first paragraph; publisher PDF p. 11 (one-based).

proposals.relationship: Deloria identifies a tension in Wilson’s oral-history argument between shared practices for checking accuracy and an epistemology that challenges Western historical knowledge (2002).
proposals.evidence_note: Qualified methodological reception within his recognition of Native historical authority. His characterization of purity and difference is attributed to him; it does not replace Wilson’s own situated family/community claims or her recorded acknowledgment of archival scholarship’s value and limits.
primary_locators: Historiography, printed p. 20, paragraph beginning This multivalent reality, read with the two preceding paragraphs; publisher PDF p. 15.

proposals.relationship: As Gonzalez, Modzelewski, Panich and Schneider explain, Wilson credits Fanon’s writing on decolonization with helping her articulate her own struggle in Reclaiming Our Humanity (2004).
proposals.evidence_note: Explicitly mediated through the four named authors’ substantive 2006 account, read in an institutional repository. They also credit Paulo Freire’s work on praxis; his contribution is not reassigned to Fanon. Wilson’s original 2004 chapter remains unread here, and her family and community sources of knowledge retain their independent standing.
primary_locators: Institutional repository Abstract, first paragraph, especially sentence naming Fanon and Freire and distinguishing decolonization from praxis. Article citation: American Indian Quarterly 30(3–4) (2006): 388–415; original page of this passage not independently verified.
